commit.message:
Define the type aliases Buffer and RNG in a single module

Buffer and RNG were defined again in each module that uses them
(63 and 10 copies). They are now in Crypto.Util._typing, which
imports nothing from Crypto, so that any module can import it.

Decode the body of PEM blocks in constant time

binascii.a2b_base64() maps each character through a 256-byte table:
the address of each lookup depends on the private key, which leaks
through the cache.

- New C function base64_decode() (Crypto.Util._base64), which computes
  the value of each character with masks, and only branches on the
  position of whitespace and padding. The size of the output buffer
  is passed and checked explicitly.
- PEM.decode() only parses the boundaries and the encapsulated headers
  as text: str.split(), str.strip() and \s in regular expressions also
  use lookup tables, so they no longer run on the body.
- ML-DSA and ML-KEM look for "Proc-Type:" in the headers only, and not
  in the whole text (the substring search branches on each character).
RSA, DSA: reject private keys in OpenSSH export
Add fast path to CTR mode for short bytes messages
Docs: smaller headings for the FAQ questions
Docs: list SSE2 among the CPU extensions
Docs: revise features page and its layout
Fix potential side-channel on H multiplication

Add AES-GCM-SIV mode (RFC 8452)

POLYVAL uses new ghash_rev_* functions, which skip the block byte swap of GHASH.

HPKE: only advance the sequence number when unseal() succeeds

A ciphertext rejected by unseal() still consumed a sequence number, so a
single forged message made every later message of the context fail.
RFC 9180, Section 5.2, increments the sequence only after Open succeeds.

Add the curve secp256k1, and low_s for ECDSA

Support secp256k1 in Crypto.PublicKey.ECC, Crypto.Signature.DSS and
Crypto.Protocol.DH, with Wycheproof vectors. It is not accepted by HPKE and
OpenSSH, which define no use for it.

GH#759: add the parameter low_s to DSS.new (all curves).

Also encode DER signatures faster, and fix the import of OpenSSH keys: reject
a curve that does not match the key type, and raise ValueError (not TypeError)
for unsupported or malformed public keys.
Docs: document cipher objects of each mode of operation
Fix docs build: use python3, mock AESNI functions
Fix test_pkcs1_ct on ARM64: no comparison of secret positions with error values

Add the test vectors of draft-irtf-cfrg-rsa-guidance for implicit rejection

The 48 test vectors in Appendix B of draft-irtf-cfrg-rsa-guidance-10
(keys of 2048, 2049, 3072 and 4096 bits), used by test_pkcs1_15.py.

Constant-time check of the PKCS#1 v1.5 and OAEP decoding

New test test_pkcs1_ct runs src/pkcs1_decode.c under Valgrind memcheck
(64 and 32 bits), with the decrypted EM, DB, AM and candidate lengths
marked as secret, as test_nat_ct does for the nat library.

It found two secret-dependent branches in oaep_decode(), both fixed:
- the final result was selected with a branch on the padding check:
  it is now selected with safe_select_idx(), and 0 (instead of -1)
  means incorrect padding (the only caller treats both as errors);
- with gcc -O1..-O3, the comparison with the position of the 0x01 byte
  let gcc rewrite the loop counter as i - one_pos: it now uses ct_lt()
  and ct_mask() from nat_ct.h, with a barrier on i.

select_alt_length() uses the same helpers, and the dead memset of
eq_mask is removed.
Use implicit rejection for PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption
Add comment about slowdown on simpler AArch64 cores
Require ARMv8 SHA-512 on Windows ARM64 CI; NEON Keccak with MSVC
Split the SHA-2 compression functions out of hash_SHA2_template.c
Use the ARMv8 SHA-256 and SHA-512 instructions for SHA-2
EC: invert field elements with the power for public exponents

Faster RSA: public exponents, cached Montgomery contexts, cheaper blinding

Modular exponentiation with a public exponent (a public Integer, now
the RSA public exponent) uses the value of the exponent instead of
the constant-time fixed window: binary method up to 64 bits, windows
read directly otherwise. The time still does not depend on the base.

An odd modulus keeps its Montgomery context (nat_mont_new), so R^2
mod n is computed once. nat_powmod_ctx() and nat_mulmod_ctx() use it
with private scratchpads, so threads can share it; the caller keeps a
reference to the context during the C call. Integer._mul_mod() is a
modular multiplication with two Montgomery products instead of a
product and a division.

RSA private operations: the blinding pair (r^e, r^-1) is squared
between uses, with a new random r every 32 uses and after a fork
(as OpenSSL does), instead of a new r^e and r^-1 each time. The check
against faults in PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS signing uses the public exponent
path instead of Python's pow().

The MULX/ADX row of the Montgomery products addresses memory with a
base and a displacement (an index register makes Intel cores split
MULX and ADCX into more micro-ops), and it is not inlined: with one
copy per caller, the copies used to evict each other from the micro-op
cache when squarings and multiplications alternate, and 75-80% of the
micro-ops came from the legacy decoders. The table scan of mont_pow
is done word by word. Montgomery products are about 20% faster.

x86-64 (i5), master -> this commit, in us:
  RSA-2048 sign 1063 -> 624, verify 83 -> 43
  RSA-3072 sign 2664 -> 1709, verify 137 -> 57
  RSA-4096 sign 5356 -> 3474, verify 209 -> 77
  DSA-2048 sign 344 -> 262, verify 585 -> 431

Mark the RSA modulus and the DSA subgroup order as public

Both are public values. As public Integer objects, they let
random_range() use its fast path for public bounds: the RSA blinding
factor (18 -> 11 us for 2048 bits) and the DSA nonce and blinding
factor. DSA-2048 signing is about 4% faster, RSA-2048 signing about 1%.

Only n and q are flagged: the private components, and the values
derived from them, are still not public.

Faster Integer.random_range() for public bounds

When both bounds are public (Python ints or public Integers, like the
order of an ECC group), compute the size of the interval with Python
integers instead of three Integer operations, and compare the shifted
candidate with the upper bound directly. The candidate stays an
Integer, so the secret value is still handled in constant time, and
the output is the same for the same random bytes.

random_range() over the P-256 order: 16 -> 8 us. ECDSA P-256 signing
about 13% faster, ECC key generation about 35% (x86).

Run the constant-time C tests on the Linux ARM64 CI

The test_c_linux_arm job did not install Valgrind, so CMake silently
skipped the constant-time tests (test_nat_ct, test_ec_nat_ct and the
curve and DES ones). They pass on AArch64 with gcc and clang.
Mention KangarooTwelve among the functions that use several threads

Speed up CTR mode

XOR the key stream 16 bytes at a time instead of byte by byte, call
add_le()/add_be() directly instead of through a function pointer, and
advance the counters of a batch with a fast path when only their least
significant byte changes. CTR is 2.5-3.5x faster on large data (x86
with AES-NI, and ARMv8), and GCM about 2x.

Test CTR in place, too.

Speed up the ARMv8 AES and GHASH code

AES: use the round keys in place instead of copying them on each call,
and split the single-block round loop like the 8-block one (first 9
rounds, then the rest), so that compilers unroll it. Single-block
modes are faster: CBC decryption 1.4x, OFB 1.25x on a Graviton3.

GHASH: reduce once every 8 blocks (instead of 4), accumulating the
partial products, with one loop for full and partial groups (GMAC 1.25x).

Move the Changelog entry of the branch to 4.3.0.

Fix GH#954: OBJECT IDENTIFIER incorrectly decoded

when the first byte of an arc is 0x80

or when the the last byte of the last arc has bit 7 set
Upgrade cibuildwheel, add wheels for PyPy 3.12
Pin Ubuntu to 24.04 to support Python 3.9
Use the ARMv8 Cryptography Extensions for AES and GHASH

Update the Wycheproof test vectors to commit d17cc89f

New Ed25519 tests and the new chacha20_counter_test.json.
XChaCha20 keeps its 32-bit block counter (draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha),
so the vectors beyond 2^32 blocks are expected to fail.
Fix unused parameter warning in ed25519_new_point
Fix MSVC warnings C4267, C4295, C4388 and C4389
Avoid MSVC warning C4746 on ARM: ISO volatile intrinsics

Fix PyPy wheels on Windows with setuptools 84.2

Build the PyPy extensions without py_limited_api: setuptools 84.2 names
them .pyd on Windows, which PyPy cannot find.

See https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/5367
Don't run portable python with cffi
Add import and export of ML-KEM keys (RFC 9935)

Drop the hybrid KEMs MLKEM768-P256 and MLKEM1024-P384

Only X-Wing (MLKEM768-X25519) is kept: the definition of the other two
hybrid KEMs (draft-irtf-cfrg-concrete-hybrid-kems) may still change.
Their implementation is in the previous commit, to restore once the
drafts are final.
Add ML-KEM, hybrid KEMs and post-quantum HPKE
Use our own keccak code for MLDSA
Faster scalar Keccak permutation (plane by plane, 2 rounds per iteration)
